payload.text: The Brennecke Institute developed a thalliline-doped sodium-flow battery intended to reduce electrolyte crossover, a key aging mechanism in sodium-flow systems. An independent teardown audit corrected the prototype’s cycle life to 8,400 cycles to the 80% capacity knee, retracting the earlier 12,000-cycle claim because it used un-normalized depth-of-discharge. The battery’s gravimetric energy density is 148 Wh/kg, and its projected stack-level cost is $61/kWh at 500 MWh manufacturing scale. Its operating-temperature floor is 4 °C, below which the thalliline dopant precipitates from the negative electrolyte and cycling must stop.

FLAGS: superseded cycle-life values: Source A and unpublished pre-audit draft state “12,000 cycles,” while finalized Source C governs with “8,400 cycles.”
VERDICT: APPROVE
